title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent to Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench (study_id rX4f7-1), a paired evaluation comparing a one‑shot NL→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline using the same shared initial candidate across 1,200 intent→config episodes. Using the requested model gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and Mininet‑style emulation, we applied a preregistered binary episode success rule (validator accepts final config AND emulator shows no availability degradation above tolerance AND no automatic rollback). We completed 1,199 paired observations. Baseline success = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149291076; guarded success = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0. The paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000). Provider audit shows model_calls_used = 1,203 and repair calls = 3. The preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis H3 (per‑cluster breakdown) was not executed; only pooled confirmatory analysis is archived (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json). Under the chosen synthetic corpus and validator settings baseline performance was near ceiling, which constrained headroom for measurable guarded improvements. All run artifacts, seeds, and analysis code are archived to enable exact reproduction.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs have been proposed to translate operator intent in natural language into executable device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Prior surveys and system reports emphasize that operational reliability depends on the orchestration stack—LLM plus verifiers, provenance, and sandboxed execution—rather than the base LLM alone. Generate–validate–repair (verifier‑assisted) pipelines are a canonical mitigation: an LLM proposes a candidate, an automated verifier enforces syntactic/semantic constraints, and a repair loop iterates until verifier acceptance. Despite conceptual support for such guarded workflows, there is limited preregistered, paired evidence measuring whether verifier assistance yields an operationally meaningful improvement on a rollback‑aware binary success metric relative to one‑shot generation. We address this gap with NetOpsTraceBench: a preregistered, emulator‑grounded, paired study that isolates verifier/repair effects by sharing the same initial candidate across conditions.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers frame LLMs as components inside AIOps/NetOps workflows and repeatedly call for workflow‑centered evaluation (trace quality, verifier interactions, rollback semantics) rather than isolated one‑shot QA benchmarks [http://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12708/229494; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13389]. Concrete verifier‑assisted approaches appear in adjacent domains (NL→formal spec generation, topology compilation) and NetOps prototypes that instrument deterministic parsers and rule sets to accept/reject candidates and to drive repairs [http://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09369; https://doi.org/10.3390/app16010085]. Empirical studies document LLM failure modes—hallucination, incorrect semantics/units, overconfidence/miscalibration, provenance loss, prompt‑injection vulnerability—that motivate external verification and provenance linkers [https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6947162; https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7222278; https://doi.org/10.20935/acadai8260]. These works show feasibility of verifier loops but also highlight dependence on task selection, verifier strictness, and dataset construction; NetOpsTraceBench operationalizes a preregistered, artifact‑rich paired comparison to make such dependencies observable and reproducible.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimands: The study was preregistered (rX4f7-1; preregistration manifest SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712) and froze hypothesis H1 (primary: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), H2 (failure‑mode cataloging), and H3 (confirmatory per‑topology cluster breakdown). The primary estimand is the paired difference in binary episode success (guarded − baseline). The prespecified analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1 with α=0.05; power planning targeted a 5 percentage‑point MDE under assumed baseline ≈0.70 and discordant‑pair rates recorded in the preregistration.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes: The run completed 2,398 of 2,400 planned episodes producing complete_pair_count = 1,199. Analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json). Observed counts: n11 = 1,196 (both succeeded), n10 = 3 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. From these counts baseline_success_rate = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149291076; guarded_success_rate = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0. Estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446. Because outcomes are binary and concentrated in concordant cells, the confirmatory executor used an exact McNemar two‑sided test; archived p = 0.25. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000) = [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957]. Provider and execution accounting (execution/execution_manifest.json and deterministic_reconciliation.json) record model_calls_used = 1,203 and repair‑stage calls = 3 (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 1,200; repair = 3). Missingness artifacts report failed_baseline_episodes = 1, failed_guarded_episodes = 1, both_missing_pairs = 1, yielding the 1,199 complete pairs used.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and why H3 is unresolved: The pooled confirmatory analysis shows no statistically significant advantage for the guarded pipeline given this corpus and verifier setting (p = 0.25; 95% CI includes zero). Two archived, artifact‑grounded explanations are supported. First, baseline one‑shot performance was near ceiling (≈99.75%), which reduced headroom and made the preregistered MDE (5 pp) unattainable in practice; the observed absolute gain ≈0.25 pp is too small for the planned sensitivity. Second, task generation and validator design materially affected repair invocation: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced synthetic tasks with explicit required sequences and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted the majority of shared initial candidates (validation_after.valid = true in representative scoring artifacts), so automatic repair was rarely triggered (repair = 3). Preregistered confirmatory H3 (topology‑cluster breakdown across 'edge' vs 'core') was not executed; only pooled confirmatory analysis was produced and archived. The absence of per‑cluster confirmatory artifacts is reflected in the archived analysis outputs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json) and in the deterministic reconciliation artifacts. Researchers should therefore not interpret the pooled null result as a per‑cluster inference: follow‑up work or sensitivity runs (varying corpus adversariality and verifier strictness or executing the preregistered cluster breakdown) are required to evaluate topology‑specific effects.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench, a paired, emulator‑grounded comparison of one‑shot and verifier‑assisted NL→configuration pipelines using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. On 1,199 complete pairs the guarded pipeline increased absolute success by ≈0.25 percentage points (estimate = 0.0025020851) but this difference was not statistically significant (exact McNemar p = 0.25; 95% CI includes zero). Provider audit (model_calls_used = 1,203; repair calls = 3) and validator traces show repair was rarely invoked because the shared initial candidate frequently met verifier checks. Preregistered per‑topology confirmatory hypothesis H3 was not executed; only pooled analysis artifacts are archived. The archived artifacts, seeds, and analysis code permit exact reproduction and form a basis for targeted sensitivity studies that vary task ambiguity, verifier strictness, and model families to identify conditions where verifier scaffolding yields operationally meaningful improvements.

limitations: Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.
Task corpus skew: synthetic/consented tasks yielded near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture all deployment failure modes (routing convergence, vendor idiosyncrasies, transient telemetry).

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon signed‑rank paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test because outcomes were binary. This deviation is recorded in the archived analysis artifacts and in the Disclosure Statement above.
Operational external validity: absence of heterogeneous vendor renderers, real production templates, and live rollouts constrain direct production generalization.
